subject: Copalytics: eval ops plan, recommended models, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@copalytics.ai>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@copalytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + Ops plan: Copalytics eval & model recommendations

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today — helpful to see the sample intents and the edge-case examples you flagged. Quick recap and an operational plan for running a customer-specific eval on Redwood so we can converge on a model fit recommendation.

Summary of recommendations (short):
- Candidate models to benchmark: Redwood-OpenChat-13B (q4_0), Llama-2-70B-chat (8-bit), Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8). Start with the 13B q4_0 for fast iteration, then run the 70B for high-recall comparisons.
- Quantization profile: run q4_0 and int8 variants where available; we’ll surface per-token quality deltas in the report.
- Prompt bank: use the two prompt sets attached (copalytics_eval_prompts_v1.jsonl) + your sample dataset. We’ll include negative prompts for hallucination testing.

Benchmarks & artifacts:
- Preliminary perf snapshot (internal): https://redwood.console/benchmarks/copalytics-20261130
- Shared workspace with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-copalytics-eval (contains prompt sets and run templates)

Dataset format we need for the initial run: CSV or JSONL, one row per example. Minimum columns for CSV: id, prompt, expected_answer, label_type (classification|generation), metadata. Example: "123, "What’s the billing code for X?", "99213", classification, {"product":"claims"}"

Scoring rubric (high level):
- Classification tasks: accuracy, precision/recall, confusion sample for false positives.
- Generation tasks: exact-match rate, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, semantic similarity (BERTScore) when labels are fuzzy, and hallucination flags (manual review on a 200-example sample).
- Operational: latency p50/p95, throughput (tokens/sec), and run cost estimate per 1k requests.

Assumptions & constraints we flagged:
- If dataset contains PHI: we need to run in either Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) or Private (VPC/on-prem) — we can support both.
- For typical enterprise evals we keep datasets for 30 days unless you request otherwise; retention is configurable.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a 200–500 example sample CSV (anonymized if PHI) — use the attached copalytics_sample_dataset.csv as a template.
2) We run a first-pass eval on Redwood-OpenChat-13B (q4_0) and return a report with per-prompt results + summary.
3) Decide whether to run the 70B run for high-recall benchmark.

Available kickoff windows (PST): Wed 12/8 9–11am, Thu 12/9 1–3pm. Tell me which works and we’ll lock in Marissa (CS) for ops.

Attachments: copalytics_eval_prompts_v1.jsonl, copalytics_sample_dataset.csv

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool in our infra with customer isolation guarantees; faster to start (24–48 hours) but traffic flows through Redwood network.

2) SOC2 + evidence: link to SOC2 report and control matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-copalytics-eval (see SOC2/Redwood-SOC2-2026.pdf). I’ve also added the standard DPA and retention terms there.

3) On-prem eval tooling: yes — we can provide the eval runner (scorer_template.py) and prompt bank so you can run locally and share aggregated metrics only. If you choose that path we’ll still request a kickoff to align scoring thresholds and tie the scoring code to the exact prompt versions.

4) Attached for convenience: eval_spec_template.csv (simple column/label spec you can use to format the sample), and I’ve uploaded a short runbook we’ll use during the session.

HubSpot record: HS-987654 — I’ll log the kickoff and milestones there.

See you Thu 12/9 1pm PST — I’ll send a calendar invite and include the call agenda (data format, scoring thresholds, privacy option).

Jordan —

I’ll own the ops side for the kickoff. Quick notes for the run so we’re aligned:
- Accepted formats: CSV (utf-8) or JSONL. Minimal required columns: id, prompt, expected_answer, label_type, confidence_label (optional).
- Scorer options: we’ll run both deterministic metrics (exact match, accuracy) and semantic metrics (BERTScore). I’ll attach scorer_template.py and a short eval_runbook.md with the steps I’ll run during the session.
- Regression monitoring: we’ll enable quality regression alerts tied to this prompt set (baseline from the 13B q4_0 run). I suggest we set an initial guardrail of a 5% drop on exact-match for critical intents and a 10% drop for optional intents; we can tune on the follow-up review.
- Ops constraints: if they require Private on-prem, book a 2–4 day window for deployment and confirm access method (SFTP / HTTPS ingest). If Dedicated, we can start in 24–48 hours and keep artifacts in the customer workspace for 30 days.

I’ll be on the Thu 12/9 1pm PST call and will bring the run checklist.
